title: AlphaAgents: Large Language Model based Multi-Agents for Equity Portfolio Constructions

task.value: Using role-based LLM multi-agent collaboration and debate to support stock selection in equity research and portfolio management under different risk tolerances.
task.quote: This study investigates the application of role-based multi-agent systems to support stock selection in equity research and portfolio management.

architecture.value: Three specialist agents (Fundamental with 10-K/yfinance pull and RAG tools, Sentiment with news summarization tool, Valuation with volatility/return tool) coordinated by an AutoGen group chat assistant; round-robin debate until consensus; risk profiles set via prompts.
architecture.quote: We utilize the Microsoft AutoGen framework (Wu et al., 2023) as the infrastructure for our multi-agent system, leveraging its group chat and assistant agent capabilities.

data.value: 10-K and 10-Q disclosures, Bloomberg financial news, and Yahoo Finance historical price and volume data; universe of 15 randomly selected technology-sector stocks.
data.quote: The primary data sources utilized in the system are listed in Table 1, including 10-K and 10-Q financial disclosures, Bloomberg financial news, and historical stock price and volume data from Yahoo Finance.

window.value: Agents used data and news from January 2024; portfolios initialized February 1, 2024 and monitored over the following four months.
window.quote: The agents were trained using data and news from January 2024. Based on each agent’s responses and their final decisions following debate and collaboration, we constructed the corresponding portfolios: the valuation agent portfolio, news sentiment agent portfolio, fundamental agent portfolio, and the final multi-agent portfolio, all initialized on February 1, 2024.

models.value: GPT4o as the LLM; GPT 4-o also cited as embedding model in the RAG tool.
models.quote: After experimenting with various GPT models, we chose GPT4o as the model for our experiments.

baselines.value: Equal-weighted benchmark portfolio of the 15 tech stocks, and single-agent portfolios from the fundamental and valuation agents.
baselines.quote: For comparison, single-agent portfolios from the fundamental and valuation agents were also created; the sentiment agent was excluded due to insufficient news coverage in some cases.

headline_result.value: Qualitative only: in the risk-neutral setting the multi-agent portfolio outperformed the benchmark and single-agent portfolios over the test window; in the risk-averse setting all agent portfolios underperformed the benchmark.
headline_result.quote: In the risk-neutral setting, the proposed multi-agent outperforms the benchmark as well as the single agent framework during the testing window.

limitations.value: Analysis limited in scope; risk-seeking prompts indistinguishable from risk-neutral; sentiment agent lacked news coverage for some stocks; focus only on stock selection, not portfolio optimization.
limitations.quote: While a risk-seeking profile was also tested, its outputs were nearly indistinguishable from the risk-neutral case and excluded from final evaluation highlighting a limitation of prompt-based differentiation for adjacent risk profiles.
